report:
Based on my research, the evidence does **not** support the claim that prolonged use of cloth or surgical masks causes dangerous carbon dioxide (CO₂) buildup in healthy individuals.

**Evidence against the claim:**

- The CDC and multiple health authorities have stated that CO₂ molecules are far smaller than viruses and pass easily through cloth or surgical masks, so dangerous trapping does not occur ([USA Today Fact Check](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2021/10/29/fact-check-face-masks-dont-create-dangerous-co-2-children/6182627001/)).
- A 2021 study in *BMC Infectious Diseases* measured CO₂ under various masks and found that while levels increased slightly, they **remained below short-term exposure limits** ([Springer/BMC](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12879-021-06056-0)).
- The Cleveland Clinic concluded it is "not possible" to inhale dangerous amounts of CO₂ while wearing a cloth or disposable mask ([Cleveland Clinic](https://health.clevelandclinic.org/can-wearing-a-mask-make-you-sick)).
- AP and Reuters fact-checks found no evidence that mask-wearing causes hypercapnia (excess CO₂ in the blood) in healthy adults or children ([AP News](https://apnews.com/article/archive-fact-checking-8949990001); [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/article/fact-check/covid-19-face-masks-do-not-trap-dangerous-levels-of-carbon-dioxide-idUSL1N2T01U3/)).

**Evidence cited in favor of the claim:**

- A 2023 German scoping review (published in *Heliyon*) reported CO₂ under masks could reach 1.41–3.2% of inhaled air, calling for more research on long-term exposure, though it acknowledged levels were "usually within short-term exposure limits" ([ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405844023013245)).
- A 2021 study in *JAMA Pediatrics* claimed dangerous CO₂ levels in masked children, but it was **retracted** due to serious methodological flaws ([Retraction Watch](https://retractionwatch.com/2021/07/08/authors-of-widely-panned-study-of-masks-in-children-respond-to-critics/)).

**Conclusion:** While masks can cause a small, measurable increase in CO₂ behind the mask, the overwhelming evidence indicates this does not reach dangerous levels for healthy adults or children during prolonged use. The strongest studies supporting the claim have been retracted or acknowledged that levels remain within safety limits.
